answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to answer a private whisper prompt tied to a network beacon every epoch. The response must incorporate a gale-scale sequential hash chain that consumes 12 minutes of single-threaded CPU time. An attacker spawning 200 clones must therefore provision 200 dedicated cores simultaneously, spending approximately $1.20 in spot-instance fees per epoch with no parallelization possible, whereas a single honest agent pays only its normal operating cost. Any cloned answer that fails the timing window loses its attestation weight entirely.
